# HEVC reference-control trace

**AI disclosure:** This document, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI at the contributor's request.

This is the opt-in trace and offline checker delivered for
[libva-v4l2_request#84](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/84),
the bounded offline child of [#42](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/42)
(RPS_E). It records the HEVC reference controls **as the driver actually
submitted them** so that two client paths can be compared request by request.
It changes nothing about reference ordering or decode behaviour, it draws no
conclusion about the RPS_E cause, and it is not a hardware capture: the
recorded evidence in this repository is from the offline in-memory device only.

## Enabling

| `LIBVA_V4L2_HEVC_REFTRACE` | Effect |
|---|---|
| unset or empty | Off. One relaxed atomic load and ordinal bookkeeping per submitted request, nothing written. |
| `stderr` | One JSON line per queued request on standard error. |
| any other value | Regular-file path, opened for append without following a blocking FIFO open; descriptor closes on exec. |

A non-regular or unusable path disables the trace and writes one `client` diagnostic with
`op: hevc-reftrace`; the value itself is never echoed. `LIBVA_V4L2_DIAG` and
`LIBVA_V4L2_TRACE` are independent and unchanged. Write/flush failure disables further
tracing and reports an incomplete capture without changing the decode status. Use
a fresh regular file per process/campaign; stderr can experience pipe backpressure.

Enabling the trace never changes the controls or the VA status: the
`hevc-reftrace-*` tests submit the same pictures with the trace off and on
through an intercepting device and require byte-identical
`VIDIOC_S_EXT_CTRLS` payloads and identical statuses. A request the kernel
rejects produces no record.

## Records

Schema identifier: `libva-v4l2request.hevc-refs/1`. One record per request
the driver queued (`MEDIA_REQUEST_IOC_QUEUE` accepted), written after the
queue call returns. A picture that the backend splits into several
slice-batch requests produces one record per request with the same `pic`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema`, `run`, `seq` | Schema tag; the 16-hex-digit per-process run identifier shared with `docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md`; record number from 1 within the run. |
| `ctx`, `va_context` | The diagnostics context serial (never reused) and the client's VA context ID. |
| `pic`, `req` | Decode-order picture ordinal and request ordinal within the context, both from 1 and counted from context creation even if the trace is enabled later. |
| `first`, `last` | Whether this request carried the picture's first slice batch and its last one. |
| `target` | CAPTURE buffer index the picture decodes into (context-local small integer). |
| `poc`, `irap`, `idr` | `pic_order_cnt_val` and the IRAP/IDR flags from the decode parameters. |
| `ltr_sps` | SPS `long_term_ref_pics_present_flag` for this picture. |
| `reorder` | 1 when the AVD decode-order remap (`docs/RPS_E.md`, r8) was applied to this picture's DPB, i.e. an AVD context with `ltr_sps` 0. |
| `total_curr` | `NumPicTotalCurr` derived for the slice headers. |
| `dpb[]` | The `V4L2_CID_STATELESS_HEVC_DECODE_PARAMS` DPB in submitted slot order: `i` slot, `buf` the CAPTURE buffer index named by the entry's timestamp (`-1` if none), `poc`, `lt` long-term flag, `field` field-pic flag. |
| `st_before`, `st_after`, `lt_curr` | `poc_st_curr_before`, `poc_st_curr_after` and `poc_lt_curr`, as DPB slot indices. |
| `slices[]` | Each `V4L2_CID_STATELESS_HEVC_SLICE_PARAMS` element in the request: `i`, `type` (`I`/`P`/`B`), `nal` unit type, `l0`/`l1` reference lists as DPB slot indices, `tmvp`, and when `tmvp` is 1 `col_l0` and `col` (collocated list and index). At most 16 slices are listed; `slices_omitted` counts the rest. A decoder without the slice-parameter control produces an empty list. |
| `error` | Only on a record that could not be formatted within its bound (`record-overflow`); the identity fields are still present. |

A DPB slot is identified by `buf`, and the picture that wrote that buffer is
the most recent earlier record in the same context with `last` 1 and the same
`target`. The checker performs that resolution, so two clients with different
buffer allocation still correlate. No record carries bitstream bytes, physical
addresses, pointers, file names or media paths; every value is a small integer
derived from the control structures, and a record is at most 4096 bytes.

## Offline differential checker

`tests/hevc-reftrace-check.py` compares two trace files:

```sh
python3 tests/hevc-reftrace-check.py validate trace-a.jsonl
python3 tests/hevc-reftrace-check.py compare trace-a.jsonl trace-b.jsonl [--context A B] [--expected-pictures N] [--json]
```

Exit status 0 means the recorded reference fields in the captured pictures are
equal (or the trace is structurally valid); 1 reports a recorded difference;
2 rejects incomplete, malformed or ambiguous input. With no independently
supplied `--expected-pictures`, equality is explicitly **captured-prefix only**:
loss of a whole final record cannot be detected from JSON lines alone. For the
300-picture RPS_E/RPS_B captures, require `--expected-pictures 300` plus successful
client/guard completion and output-frame evidence. Even that does not attest
fields this trace does not record.

The checker validates bounded JSON, unique keys, numeric/boolean ranges, slot
indices, sequential ordinals and complete first/last slice-batch boundaries.
Overflow markers, omitted slices and references not attributable to an earlier
record are rejected rather than equated to another unknown. Different CAPTURE
allocations are normalized to their prior picture identity; DPB slot order stays
significant. Unknown fields are retained for comparison. `reorder` is client
provenance rather than a submitted control, so its value does not by itself
establish a control difference. Multi-context input requires explicit selection.

Records compare only this selected reference-control subset. They omit other
SPS/PPS fields, weights, entry-point offsets and bitstream contents. Matching
records therefore do not prove that all userspace inputs match or isolate the
kernel/firmware as the cause. Output hashes and additional discriminating
observations remain necessary.

## Associating a later capture with the RPS_E output mismatches

Actual captures on hardware are parent-#42 work and need the guarded
procedure in `tests/README.md`; nothing below has been run on a decoder.
When they happen, the association works like this:

1. **VA path.** Run the strict conformance path for `RPS_E_qualcomm_5` with
   `LIBVA_V4L2_HEVC_REFTRACE=<file>` and the frame comparison that produces
   the output-order mismatch indices in `docs/RPS_E.md` (first VA mismatch is
   output frame 31). Output-order indices are not decode-order request IDs:
   retain an explicit parser/decoder association between output-frame index,
   decode-order picture identity and POC (including IDR/POC-reset epochs).
   FFmpeg `showinfo` output indexes or timestamps alone do not provide that
   mapping. Locate the matching trace picture only after this association has
   been independently established; do not treat output indices 26/31 as request
   ordinals or assume POC is unique across the whole stream. Its `pic`/`req` and its `dpb[]`, `st_*`/`lt_curr` and
   `slices[].l0/l1` are the controls that produced the wrong picture; the
   earlier records named by `buf` are the references it used.
2. **Direct V4L2 path.** GStreamer `v4l2slh265dec` does not use this driver, so
   it produces no record of this schema. A comparable trace has to be
   recorded at its own control-submission boundary in the same field
   layout (the schema is deliberately built only from V4L2 control contents,
   so an independent writer can populate it). Once such a file exists,
   `compare` reports the first request where the two encodings diverge.
3. **Reading the result.** A difference in `dpb[].src`/`poc`/`lt` or in
   `st_*`/`lt_curr` before the first mismatching picture points at reference
   encoding to investigate; equal records only rule out differences in the
   fields actually captured, not other client inputs. The conclusion belongs in #42, with
   the capture attached; this document only defines how to line the data up.

The r8 `RPS_B` remap and the SPS-based long-term gate are unchanged by this
work, and no stream is treated specially.


## Maintainer adversarial review

Before integration, seven synthetic invalid/incomplete traces were reproduced as
false equality and picture ordinal zero crashed the checker. Regression coverage
now includes those cases, duplicate keys, unknown-null fields, malformed ranges,
batch ownership, expected capture extent and implicit P-slice collocated L0.
A FIFO destination also reproduced a blocked client, and `/dev/full` reproduced
silent write failure; both have offline regressions with unchanged submitted
control bytes and successful decode statuses. Contributor work received separate
maintainer review; maintainer corrections were self-reviewed. These fixes provide
investigation tools and do not establish the RPS_E cause or a new hardware pass.
